cohort: Regular English-taught BSc International Business, RIO 50019, September route.

courseDetails.name: Global Supply Chain Management
courseDetails.content: Contemporary organizations are part of global networks. The perspective of this course is to understand the role of companies in such global networks of international suppliers and buyers. The main topics treated are supply strategy, outsourcing, characteristics of both service and manufacturing organizations, distribution and after sales operations. In addition to these aspects a number of decision support tools will be presented to evaluate supply chain performance and to analyze and design flows of goods and services.

courseDetails.name: Introduction to International Business
courseDetails.content:
The course introduces students to international business and globalization. Using key theories and concepts in international business, students develop an understanding of the success and failure of multinational enterprises. These theories are applied to topics such as market opportunity assessment, internationalization strategies, entry modes, international production, marketing, finance, and corporate social responsibility. Throughout the course, students apply theories and concepts to a range of case assignments.

The case assignments help students develop analytical skills by interpreting and analysing business information and by applying theories and concepts to business cases. Students work with a range of information sources to better understand business situations and learn how international business theories can help explain firm behaviour and decisions. Students also practice drawing conclusions and communicating their findings in a clear and structured way.

Students work in diverse teams on collaborative assignments. In doing so, they develop competencies related to collaboration and teamwork, communication, and intercultural awareness. The course provides an early opportunity to work in an international and multicultural setting.

courseDetails.name: Organizational Structure
courseDetails.content: In the lectures the main themes will be highlighted and in the tutorials the book will be studied systematically. Students give presentations, make case analysis and learn to discuss the themes with pre-described roles. With the help of feedback rules, students will practice giving and receiving constructive feedback in an intercultural context. The aim is to help improve the quality of each other's work while training essential academic skills. This course provides essential paradigmatic lenses to making sense of organizations, their activities in an (inter)national setting and the main stream of theories about this. It imparts students with the notion that diverse organizational settings require the capacity to develop appropriate decision making and planning strategies as well as structures to produce the desired organizational goals, given the organization's environment. The overview of organizational theories will show the different possibilities there might be from a theoretical point of view.

courseDetails.name: Academic and Professional Development
courseDetails.content: In this course, students take their first steps in developing the fundamental academic and professional skills essential for an international business professional. They explore their role and the contribution of an academic background in the international business environment. They learn to become the voice in the boardroom: a critical, strategic, and ethically conscious presence that informs leadership and corporate decision-making. Students will learn the basics of conducting business administration-related academic research, laying the foundation for essential skills required to complete the BSc IB programme, particularly the BSc thesis. Professional development focuses on critical thinking, effective intercultural and interdisciplinary communication, self-reflection, and self-management. An integral part of the course is its connection to the future work environment, providing students with insights into the skills they need to develop and fostering an active learning attitude.

courseDetails.name: Financial Accounting for IB
courseDetails.content: Financial accounting provides a vital service by supplying information that decision makers need to make reasoned choices among alternative uses of scarce resources in the conduct of business and economic activities. To that end, accounting measures business activities by recording data about them for future use, by processing them to useful information and by communicating them to decision makers through financial reports. The topics in this course are the administration and processing of various financial transactions, the preparation of the accounts (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement) and the analysis and interpretation of the financial performance and financial position of companies.

courseDetails.name: Organizational Behaviour for IB
courseDetails.content: To understand issues concerning human behavior in organizations, it is important to move beyond common sense understanding of human conduct. It is also essential to understand one's own role in affecting behavior in organizations, and to understand the cultural context in which behavior takes place. We first examine individual psychological processes and consider personality, attitudes, values, emotion, perception and motivation. How do we perceive the world and other people, and which biases may play a role? How can individuals be motivated to perform well? We next concentrate on group behavior and social processes. How are groups formed, and how do groups affect individual behavior? How can we create a team that functions well? Finally, we examine organizational processes, including leadership, power, culture, and organizational change. Throughout the course, special attention is devoted to international and intercultural issues. The textbook and some additional readings (information is given during tutorials) provide the background for the tutorials, and this material should consequently be read in advance of each tutorial. Weekly presentations and discussions during tutorials. In addition, participation in scientific research (1 hour) is compulsory.

courseDetails.name: Economics for IB
courseDetails.content:
This course covers the fundamentals of microeconomic theory related to production decisions and the market environment in which firms operate. Microeconomics focuses on the individual decisions firms make about production and external factors such as competition and economic policy.

Key questions include: how much a firm should produce to maximize profit, how labor and capital can be used efficiently to minimize costs, what pricing strategies work during price wars, when collusion between firms succeeds or fails, and how taxes, subsidies, or quotas affect economic welfare. We also discuss how consumers choose bundles of goods and respond to price changes.

The course provides students with tools and insights from microeconomics and game theory for a systematic analysis of these issues.

courseDetails.name: International Marketing for IB
courseDetails.content: This course aims to teach students the basics of marketing as an orientation and as a function. Besides, the additional challenges when marketing in an international or global setting are discussed as products (and services) for both consumers and businesses are increasingly competing in international or global markets. Therefore, this course aims to develop an understanding of the essence of market orientation, (international) marketing environment, (international) marketing strategy (segmentation, targeting and positioning), and the marketing mix (product, price, place, and promotion), including international issues and subsequent standardization or adaptation issues.

courseDetails.name: Statistics I for IB
courseDetails.content: This course provides students with a basic background in probability theory and statistics. Topics covered are: descriptive statistics, basics of probability theory, inference about one population, inference about comparing two populations, inference about the association between variables and simple linear regression.

courseDetails.name: International Trade and Competition
courseDetails.content: When firms cross borders to generate value added abroad, they are confronted with many environmental uncertainties. Currency values, trade barriers, curbs on international investment, and the degree of macroeconomic stability in countries where production is carried out and/or goods are traded are but a few of the factors which influence a firm's daily operations and long-term (strategic) planning. In order to allow a firm to succeed internationally, its managers must not only understand how these factors impact the firm's competitive environment, but also how they are likely to evolve in the future and why. This course introduces students to the economic theories which help understand the market forces driving the global economy, as well as discussing how governments are likely to implement economic policies and their consequences for the international economy. These insights provide an essential input to our understanding of the macro-economic environment in which international business takes place. This course deals with trade theory. The follow-up course ´Firm Location and FDI´ in semester 2B deals with the monetary and financial aspects of globalization, and the changing geography of economic activity.

courseDetails.name: Research Methodology for IB
courseDetails.content: The general aim of this course is to provide students with knowledge for conducting applied scientific business research. Managers in international organizations have all sorts of information needs: they want to know how customers think about their products, how the competition is doing, and how their employees are performing. But what are the origins of these information needs? And how can scientific research be used to fulfill these needs?  These questions are central in this course. Starting point is the structuring of applied scientific business research in 5 phases: management question, diagnosis, design, implementation, and evaluation. After it has become clear how a management problem can be explicated, attention will be paid to the development of conceptual models and to the measurement of the information needs following from these models using a survey. Important measurement concepts including validity and reliability will be discussed. Subsequently, students will analyze and report (fictitious) data based on their survey, and draw conclusions. In tutorials, students will first practice and then show that they can apply these concepts in a business context. In the end, students will have experienced the entire research process.

courseDetails.name: Sustainable Management Accounting
courseDetails.entry:
Admittance to the BSc IB, Pre-MSc Programmes FEB, Pre-MSc BA Management Accounting and Control/MAC, Pre-MSc BA Health or relevant DD-programs.

Students are advised to take the Financial Accounting course before the Management Accounting course.
courseDetails.content:
Sustainable Management Accounting (in short: SMA) is an introduction to management accounting. Financial accounting provides information used primarily by investors, creditors, and various stakeholders outside organizations. In contrast, management accounting produces information used by managers and employees within organizations. SMA is designed to teach you management accounting concepts (e.g., cost classifications) and techniques (e.g., costing, differential analysis) and help you understand why different pieces of information need to be used for different purposes.

After an introduction to management accounting and the role of management accountants, we will focus on concepts and techniques that management accountants use to produce relevant information for decision-makers. These techniques are: 1) costing, 2) cost estimation, 3) cost-volume-profit analysis, 4) budgeting and variance analysis, and 5) differential analysis. We will see how these concepts and techniques are used to make appropriate economic decisions, but we will also place particular emphasis throughout the course on how they can be used to address issues related to Corporate Social and Environmental Responsibility. Finally, you will also learn how to use MS Excel as a powerful tool to support decision-making processes.

courseDetails.name: Digital Transformation in IB
courseDetails.content: Detailed study of digital transformation with the focus on international business. Students will be trained on how to identify and resolve specific problems related to international firms operating in a global organization context and going through the process of digital transformation. There are no single, right answers. Students are trained to learn how to analyze and resolve business problems in regards how firms can deal with the digital transformation. The students will gain specific skills and experience using the hands on assignment that augments the lectures. Other topics that will be covered in the course are today's technology trends that influence the business world and the way professionals work; cultural, structural and political aspects of digital transformation; managing and implementing digital projects.

courseDetails.name: Finance & Investment for IB
courseDetails.content:
This course introduces core principles of corporate finance tailored to international business students, based on Chapters 1 to 14 of Fundamentals of Corporate Finance (Berk, DeMarzo, Harford, 6th Global Edition). It places strong emphasis on developing a deep understanding of foundational topics, including financial statement analysis, time value of money, valuation of bonds and stocks, and core capital budgeting techniques such as NPV and IRR. Students also study risk and return, portfolio theory, and are introduced to the cost of capital and its role in investment decisions. Given this focus on mastering fundamental concepts in detail, the course does not aim to provide full coverage of all corporate finance topics. More advanced topics—such as capital structure decisions, payout policy, derivatives, and Mergers & Acquisitions—are reserved for a follow-up third-year course. Together, the two courses provide a comprehensive and coherent overview of corporate finance for international business students. The curriculum of this course covers the following areas in detail:  

• Introduction of Finance Activities
• Evaluation of Financial Performance
• Time Value of Money & Valuation of Financial Securities
• Risk and Return
• Introduction to Capital Budgeting

courseDetails.name: Firm Location and FDI
courseDetails.content: The international economy confronts a firm with many uncertainties: currency values, trade barriers, curbs on international investment, and the degree of macroeconomic stability in countries where production is carried out and/or goods are traded, are but a few of the factors which influence a firm's daily operations and long-term (strategic) planning. In order to allow a firm to succeed internationally, its managers must not only understand how these factors impact the firm's competitive environment, but also how they are likely to evolve in the future and why. This course introduces students to the economic theories which help the manager understand the market forces driving the global economy, as well as the consequences of the international economy for how governments are likely to implement economic policies. These insights provide an essential input to the management decision-making process. This course deals with the monetary and financial dimensions of globalization, and the changing geography of economic activity. It follows up on the first year course 'International Trade and Competition' that focuses on trade theory.

courseDetails.name: Ethics and International Business
courseDetails.entry: Students who have already taken the course Ethics in Business and Management (EBB100A05) are not allowed to take the course Ethics and International Business
courseDetails.content: International businesses operate in diverse and sometimes conflicting cultural, legal, economic, and political environments. Climate change and sustainability policies present businesses with additional challenges. Consideration of the ethical dimensions of these challenges and the critical skills required to identify them are thus ever so crucial. This course addresses both. First, it treats normative and descriptive ethical theories that help guide disciplined thinking about the ethical problems often faced by international organisations, in the context of stakeholder theory. Second, it seeks to develop critical skills such as critical thinking, analytical writing, and collaborative teamwork which are paramount to identify, reflect upon, and communicate about these problems. The course is set up in an interactive way, devoting significant attention to relevant case studies in international business ethics.

courseDetails.name: Global Business History
courseDetails.content:
Why some countries are rich while others remain poor. The course Global Business History addresses this fundamental question by focusing on the historical evolution of the business firm—one of the key drivers of economic development.

By examining the determinants of successful entrepreneurship in the past, the course seeks to explain contemporary economic patterns, including the persistent differences in income levels across countries. Understanding how firms developed over years, decades, and even centuries often provides valuable insight into present-day economic structures and outcomes. As Winston Churchill famously noted, “The further backward you look, the further forward you can see.”

Building on this perspective, the course explores the history of the business firm from an international and comparative viewpoint. It examines how firms have evolved across different periods and regions, while also analyzing how the institutional, economic, and social environments in which businesses operate have changed over time and varied across the world.

courseDetails.name: Statistics II for IB
courseDetails.entry: Knowledge about basic statistical methods and techniques with applications in the field of business administration.
courseDetails.content: The purpose of this course is to introduce students to modern statistical techniques for answering cause-and-effect questions in business applications. Students learn to describe data and handle missing values, to make causal assumptions explicit in causal diagrams, and to estimate these effects. Several techniques will be taught: descriptive analysis, causal diagrams and identification, multiple regression analysis (including categorical variables, interactions, and robust standard errors), and fixed effects models for panel data. All analyses are carried out in Stata.

courseDetails.name: Comparative Country Studies
courseDetails.content: This course provides students with analytical tools to study and compare market and business environments in different countries. Such analytical tools will comprise both 'hard' and 'soft' perspectives to understand the nature of different national business environments. In the first half of the course, the students will study relevant literature on comparative country analysis. In the second half, which is more practical, they will compare investment conditions in two countries. In the practical part, students will first compare countries on key macroeconomic, institutional, and environmental indicators to assess strategic market conditions. Subsequently, they will approach the problem from a comparative business systems perspective, focusing on institutional influences on business systems. Such a combined analysis will help give managers and businesses a complete picture of the market and business environments in different countries.

courseDetails.name: Innovation Management in Multinationals
courseDetails.content: The course Innovation Management in Multinationals introduces the complexities of innovation management in multinational firms. Because multinational firms operate in several countries, innovation management increases in complexity. For instance, how do you organize your innovation efforts: one central R&D department or several departments in different countries? How do you encourage knowledge sharing among different locations? How do you create effective teams when the members are living in different countries, representing different cultures? This course offers an introduction to innovation management in multinational firms that is structured around several topics: (a) the innovation process, (b) business models, (c) collaboration and networks, (d) multinational teams and (e) knowledge management. The course combines plenary lectures about these themes (with lots of interesting recent examples) with practical assignments in smaller groups where students apply the knowledge gained to a specific situation (i.e. a specific company and innovation).

courseDetails.name: Qualitative Research Methods for IB
courseDetails.entry: This course builds upon the 1st year course Research Methodology. Students are expected to be familiar already with basic research concepts (e.g. conceptual modelling, empirical and regulative cycle).
courseDetails.content: Qualitative research is extensively used by researchers, and business professionals. The challenge is to perform qualitative research in a systematic and methodologically responsible way. Therefore, possessing knowledge and skills to conduct qualitative research is essential for researchers and practitioners in the field of International Business. The knowledge and skills are necessary to execute sound (qualitative) research yourself, and for interpreting and judging (qualitative) research of others. In this course some frequently used qualitative methods will be covered (for example, interviewing, case study, content analysis), and for each method the pro's and con's will be discussed. There will be also a practical assignment meant to exercise all stages of a qualitative research project, such as formulating research objectives, performing interviews, analyzing qualitative data, discussing the results and finally, reporting the complete research process in a scientific report.

courseDetails.name: Cross-cultural Management
courseDetails.entry: Only BSc IB students, FEB exchange students and Major Social Sciences students are allowed to participate.
courseDetails.content: Managers and professionals today routinely work with people from different cultural backgrounds. Cultural diversity can enrich teamwork, but it can also generate misunderstandings and conflict. A key challenge is recognizing the culturally shaped assumptions and biases we unconsciously bring to the workplace. This course develops a deeper understanding of cross-cultural management through theory, case discussions, and practical activities to assist you in your present and future cross-cultural encounters and managerial activities.

courseDetails.name: Global Political Economy
courseDetails.content: This course provides an introduction to the basic theories, history, and methods of international political economy. Its subject concerns the inter-relationship between economics and politics and how it shapes the international business environment. The course covers topics, such as the global distribution of labor and institutions of trade, development policy, gender, and the environment. The course introduces students to the main perspectives in global political economy. It aims to teach students to take an informed position in debates about globalization and responses to it.

courseDetails.name: International Business Law for IB
courseDetails.content:
This course examines how diverse legal frameworks shape and constrain international business operations. Students gain a foundational understanding of the relationship between legal systems and business strategy in global markets, where navigating multiple jurisdictions, regulatory regimes and dispute-resolution mechanisms is an essential managerial competency.

The course addresses seven key domains: international dispute settlement, including mechanisms for resolving cross-border commercial disputes; contract law, including the formation, content and enforcement of business agreements; tort law, including business liability and the remedies available to injured parties; company law, including business structures and governance requirements; competition law, including the rules designed to maintain effective competition in markets; intellectual property law, including the protection of innovation and creative works; and international trade regulation, with particular emphasis on the World Trade Organisation framework.

Through lectures, compulsory readings, case-based tutorials and group work, students develop the analytical foundation needed to identify legal issues in international business contexts, apply core legal concepts to practical scenarios, evaluate the legal implications of commercial decisions, and communicate legal analysis in clear written English.

courseDetails.name: Bachelor's Thesis IB
courseDetails.entry: 120 ECTS of the Bachelor programme IB (i.e. 60 ECTS of the 1st year courses and 60 ECTS of 2nd and/or 3rd year courses). Double degree students must have 45 ECTS of BSc IB courses (90 ECTS programs) or 65 ECTS (120 ECTS programs). Students must have an approved study programme (application through Progress 6 weeks before the start of the BA thesis project). Students must be registered for the course on Progress.
courseDetails.content: Before or at the start of the semester, several themes are announced on Brightspace. After the introduction lecture, students hand in their theme preferences and are assigned to a theme and an associated supervisor, on the basis of preferences and previous study performance. Within the theme that students have been assigned to, they identify a relevant problem. Next, students develop a research design and conduct their research individually. The theme´s supervisor sets intermediate deadlines, organizes a series of workshops and individual meetings, which allow all students to regularly discuss their thesis setup, progress and preliminary research results. Thus, they receive regular feedback both from their peers and the theme´s supervisor. At the end of the semester the students submit their bachelor´s thesis, which is a structured and balanced report that critically analyzes a relevant problem and discusses the research findings and their implications. Note that part of these meetings are in the form of a Practical Exercise, as defined by the Board of Examiners, to assess the authenticity of the student's work. If a student does not pass the practical exercises, and authenticity of the thesis cannot be guaranteed, the student will not receive a grade, and has to redo the whole course.

courseDetails.name: International Strategic Management
courseDetails.content: This course provides an insight in and understanding of the management challenges associated with developing international strategies, and managing the operations of companies whose activities stretch across national boundaries. These insights and understanding are mainly gained through theory- and case-based group discussions of the relevant literature after students have developed their own opinions.

courseDetails.name: Research Design and Data Analytics for IB
courseDetails.entry: It is crucial that students understand the basics of statistics and regression, as this course is of applied nature. This means that knowledge on technical aspects related to for example variance and regression analyses is present. In particular, this course builds on the second-year course Statistics II for IB (EBB682B05).
courseDetails.content:
The course deals with topics like measurement, descriptive statistics, regression, factor analysis, multicollinearity, and causality and applies these concepts to quantitative research in IB. The course will focus on interpretation and critical analysis of literature while using the statistical concepts mentioned before. By going through a selection of academic journal articles dealing with international business phenomena, students will familiarize themselves with the interpretation and critical analysis of existing state-of-the-art IB research.
The selected papers will be listed on Brightspace. Students may find it helpful to use the book from the second-year course Statistics II as background reading. The course material includes statistical analysis examples, using Stata as the statistical software for analysis.

courseDetails.name: International Financial Management
courseDetails.content: The International Financial Management course concentrates on the accounting and financial issues faced by multinational corporations (MNC). The course aims to address the significant accounting and financial problems that MNC may experience and propose methods that could result in possible solutions while taking institutional, cultural, and social aspects of internationalization into consideration. Specifically, this course aims to discuss: (i) the reasons for accounting diversity across countries and its consequences on performance measurement and control of MNC. (ii) Other critical accounting and financial reporting issues (such as business combination, segment reporting, etc.) faced by MNC. (iii) International Transfer Pricing (ITP) strategies and its managerial and ethical aspects for MNC. (iv) The importance of multinational capital and operational budgeting in terms of strategy implementation and social responsibility for MNC. (v) The foreign exchange risks faced by MNC by referring to the transaction, economic, and translation exposures together with potential methods through which companies can hedge themselves against such threats.

courseDetails.name: Managing International Business Organizations
courseDetails.entry: Courses in finance, accounting, marketing, organization structure and operations, international business have been followed with success.
courseDetails.content: Managing International Business Organizations (MIBO) is one of the last courses in the BSc International Business degree program. The aim of the course is to integrate the different elements of the degree program. The course bridges the gap between theory and fact-based analytical decision making, by using a business simulation game to develop students understanding of the complexity of global business operations in a dynamic competitive environment.

components: Study abroad, International Business internship or approved faculty minor
Research Design and Data Analytics for IB
progression: The 29 compulsory entries total 150 EC. The November erratum changes other programmes. First-year completion meets the positive study advice threshold and supplies the named foundation for second-year quantitative and qualitative methods. Financial Accounting precedes Sustainable Management Accounting.

The 30 EC option group belongs to the first semester of year three in the example. It is structured choice, with one of nine published options. Approved study abroad or a selective internship may also be taken in semester two, while the faculty minors run in semester one. No host curriculum or internship placement is assumed.

First-year completion and 60 higher-year IB credits are available from the first two years. Thesis supervision also requires approval of the individual study programme and registration. The final term includes analytics building on Statistics II, strategy, finance, management and the 10 EC thesis. The taught foundations required for Managing International Business Organizations have been taken.
